problem: Prior embodied agents that ask for help rely on zero-shot LLM prompting under full observability, with the environment given as error-free text. Training such agents with imitation needs expensive interleaved language and action demonstrations, and hand-designed dense rewards cannot capture question relevance.
motivation: Household robots receive ambiguous instructions and must explore under partial observability while asking few but useful questions. LLM commonsense can serve as a scalable per-step reward signal, using privileged simulator state that is available at training time, to replace human demonstrations and manual rewards.
key_idea: Fine-tune a small MLLM (LLaVA-OneVision 0.5B with a Perceiver visual-token downsampler) as a VLA policy with online DD-PPO, using per-step rewards from a Llama-3.1-8B LLM that judges whether each clarification question helps resolve ambiguity.
insight: Sparse success reward gives 0.0 SR, and success plus programmatic subgoal reward reaches only 22.4/16.5 SR versus 45.9/38.7 with LLM question rewards (Table 2). So dense, question-aware rewards are essential. RL agents ask more questions than SFT agents (QR 0.9 vs 0.8 on unseen scenes, 1.5 vs 1.1 on unseen tasks) and achieve higher SR, and raising the question budget raises SR at the cost of a higher question ratio.
method: Ask-to-Act task: single or multi-object rearrangement in Habitat 3.0 (ReplicaCAD, Spot) with under-specified instructions. It covers 7 ambiguity types (no ambiguity, attribute, spatial, size, compositional, clean clutter, preference); the agent picks from 125 skills or asks a free-form question, and an LLM answer module simulates the user.

Policy architecture: LLaVA-OneVision 0.5B; each observation is compressed to 4 visual tokens by a Perceiver and interleaved with instruction, past actions and user answers. The model autoregressively emits an action or question as text, with constrained grammar decoding and invalid outputs treated as no-op.

LLM-generated reward: Llama-3.1-8B (served with vLLM) gets privileged state, target metadata and questions so far, and outputs a binary usefulness label for each question. The same LLM produces the subgoals used in the reward.
Reward function: 10*success + 2.5*subgoal + r3*useful_question (0.5 in the example) - 0.05*exceed_budget - 0.01 per step. The question budget defaults to the minimum number of required questions K.
RL training: DD-PPO for 50M steps on 8 A40 GPUs (24 envs per GPU), with token-length-normalized action log-probabilities so long questions are not penalized.

Baselines and SFT data: zero-shot and few-shot GPT-4o with a text world graph and ReAct (full or partial observability), and GPT-4o with SoM. The SFT baseline uses about 40k successful expert trajectories built from frontier exploration plus LLM-generated questions.

setting.backbone: LLaVA-OneVision 0.5B + Perceiver (RL fine-tuned); Llama-3.1-8B Instruct as reward LLM (frozen, training only)
setting.training_data: Online RL for 50M steps in 63 ReplicaCAD training scenes, with LLM-generated rewards; no human demonstrations
setting.observation: egocentric RGB 480x640, robot joint positions, holding indicator, base egomotion, task instruction, and user answers
setting.action_space: 125 high-level oracle skills (nav, pick, place, open, close) plus free-form template-constrained ask_question
setting.privileged: none at test time (privileged simulator state is used only for reward and answer generation during training and evaluation); the WG baselines use privileged world graphs

numbers.extra: partial observability, no privileged info at test; oracle low-level skills

numbers.eval_set_note: Unseen Tasks split (novel compositions requiring more questions, unseen scenes)
numbers.extra: partial observability, no privileged info at test; oracle low-level skills

numbers_note: Ask-to-Act is the paper's own benchmark, and both of its splits are stored under 'val-unseen'. The Unseen Scenes and Unseen Tasks splits are distinguished in eval_set_note.
results: The RL-finetuned 0.5B MLLM gets 45.9/38.7 SR on unseen scenes and unseen tasks. It beats the SFT model (33.6/29.5) and vision GPT-4o+SoM (15.7/14.3) and all partial-observability baselines, including the few-shot partially observable world-graph baseline (35.5/32.2). It is comparable to the fully observable privileged world-graph baselines (41.7/39.9 zero-shot, 46.7/44.4 few-shot).
limitations: Questions are restricted to 9 templates because a 0.5B model fails on unconstrained question sampling; all skills are oracle-based.
Only 7 synthetic task types in simulation; the LLM answerer and reward depend on privileged state, and their reliability in open-ended settings is unknown.
Only a 0.5B model was trained; larger models were not explored.
builds_on: GLaMM-style Perceiver VLA grounding (Szot et al. 2024)
version: deepread-v1 (2026-09-29): full text + insight + evidence-checked numbers
